content.intro: This lesson covers Legacy Package Management in the PowerShell learning path. It expands the supplied syllabus heading into an actionable draft with a visual, a worked example, and a short knowledge check.
content.why_it_matters: Modules make functions discoverable, versioned and reusable. Keep public functions separate from private helpers, declare supported versions and dependencies, review package provenance, and prefer current resource-management guidance while documenting legacy PowerShellGet workflows separately.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety note
content_blocks.text: The main path targets modern PowerShell 7.6 LTS. Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility is labeled separately. Some providers, admin cmdlets and APIs depend on OS, module version, permissions or tenant access; the examples are static references, not proof of execution.
